ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, rectangle $ABCD$ is folded along diagonal $BD$, and point $C$ lands on point $E$. Connect $CE$ and intersect side $AD$ at point $F$. If $DF=1$ and $BC=4$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Based on the property of folding, we have $CE\perp BD$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB + \angle DFC = 90^\circ$\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC = \angle BCD = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB + \angle CDB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle CDB = \angle DFC$,\\
$\because \angle CDF = \angle BCD = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle CDF \sim \triangle BCD$,\\
$\therefore \frac{FD}{CD} = \frac{CD}{BC}$, i.e., $\frac{1}{CD} = \frac{CD}{4}$\\
$\therefore CD = 2$ (discarding the negative value)\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, $\triangle BED$ is obtained by folding $\triangle BCD$,\\
$\therefore BC = BE = AD$, $\angle CBD = \angle DBE$, $AD \parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB = \angle DBC$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADB = \angle DBE$,\\
$\therefore \angle EAD = \angle ADB = \angle DBC$,\\
$\therefore AE \parallel BD$,\\
$\therefore CE \perp AE$,\\
In $\triangle DCB$, $\tan \angle DBC = \frac{CD}{BC} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$,\\
$\because \angle EAD = \angle DBC$\\
$\therefore \tan \angle EAD = \frac{1}{2}$\\
In $\triangle AEF$, $EF = \frac{1}{2}AE$\\
By the Pythagorean theorem, $AE^2 = AF^2 - EF^2$\\
i.e., $AE^2 = (AD - FD)^2 - \left(\frac{1}{2}AE\right)^2$\\
$\therefore AE^2 = (4 - 1)^2 - \frac{1}{4}AE^2$\\
Solving yields: $AE = \boxed{\frac{6\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a rectangle, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; diagonal BD has been drawn. After folding, point C falls to the point E above. In the figure, the line segments BE and DE formed after folding can be seen, and the connecting line CE goes downward from E through side AD, intersecting AD at point F; F is located on AD near D. Reasoning: When folding along BD, C and E are symmetric with respect to the crease BD, so BD is the perpendicular bisector of CE; hence CE ⟂ BD. Because F is on AD, DF is collinear with AD, and in the rectangle AD ⟂ CD and BC ⟂ CD. From CE ⟂ BD, it can be known that ∠DFC and ∠ADB are complementary; and in the rectangle, ∠CDB and ∠ADB are also complementary, so ∠DFC = ∠CDB. Also ∠CDF = ∠BCD = 90°, therefore ΔCDF ∼ ΔBCD. From corresponding sides, FD/CD = CD/BC. Substituting FD=1 and BC=4 gives 1/CD = CD/4, so CD²=4, and taking the positive value gives CD=2. Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so AD=BC=4; folding preserves length, so DE=DC=2. Let α=∠DBC=∠ADB. In right triangle DBC, BC=4 and CD=2, so BD=√(4²+2²)=2√5, and tan α=CD/BC=1/2. Let β=∠BDC, then β=90°−α. Folding maps ∠BDC to ∠BDE, so ∠BDE=β. According to the order of the rays near point D in the figure, DE is above AD and DB is below AD; therefore ∠BDE=∠ADE+∠ADB, hence ∠ADE=β−α. From the 2-4-2√5 right triangle DBC, sin α=CD/BD=1/√5 and cos α=BC/BD=2/√5; also β=90°−α, so cos β=sin α=1/√5 and sin β=cos α=2/√5. Thus cos∠ADE=cos(β−α)=cosβ cosα+sinβ sinα=(1/√5)(2/√5)+(2/√5)(1/√5)=4/5. Applying the law of cosines in triangle ADE: AE²=AD²+DE²−2·AD·DE·cos∠ADE=4²+2²−2·4·2·(4/5)=20−64/5=36/5. Therefore AE=√(36/5)=6√5/5.
